title: The Liver Failure Behind the Falling Hemoglobin — Forensic Pathology, Diagnostic Verification & Real-World Injury/Illness Prevention

teenKit.tldr: An 18-year-old's blood cells suddenly began bursting apart, leading doctors to discover a hidden genetic disorder where her body couldn't process copper, destroying her liver from the inside out.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This case proves that symptoms in one part of the body—like crashing blood counts—can actually be a smoke screen for a totally different organ system failing.
keyTakeaways: Wilson's disease is an inherited condition that prevents the body from getting rid of excess copper, turning the liver's waste management system toxic over time.
When red blood cells burst open rapidly (hemolysis), it can dangerously mask and coincide with sudden, catastrophic liver failure.
Checking the math and diagnostic data in medical literature is essential to avoiding misdiagnoses and understanding how tests actually perform.

vocab.meaning: A terrifyingly rapid, severe collapse of liver function that happens over just a few days or weeks.
A condition where red blood cells are destroyed and removed from the bloodstream faster than the body can replace them.
The medical science of investigating sudden, suspicious, or unexplained deaths to figure out exactly what went wrong inside the body.
The strict process of double-checking lab tests and clinical evidence to make sure a medical diagnosis is 100% correct.
